title: Before Trilogy is not a Trilogy - Before Four!

commenti.body:
Linklater (and the protagonists) have talked about this a ton of times, last I heard he said he felt he missed the window to make it, but that you never say never

Ethan Hawke says he's up to it, Julie Delpy don't want to make any others movie because she's sick of the industry, you can Google it and follow the trace of interviews and quotes.

In cinema trilogies have a tradition of being based around ideas. Directors often work in trilogies which are around loose ideas rather than chronological narratives. 
 
For example Von Trier's Europa Trilogy is simply connected via them all having hazy aesthetics and being genre deconstructions - they're all vastly different, unrelated films otherwise. Pasolini had his Trilogy of Life which were all based on mediaeval literature and mainly about the human body but otherwise weren't connected in any narrative ways. 

So I think the Before trilogy is somewhat informed by this convention of cinema.

In regards to the other stuff about a fourth film, etc. They could potentially make one I'm sure and maybe in another 15-20 years it could be interesting but I do personally feel like they've pretty thoroughly explored the characters and ideas. As a viewer I don't feel like I need more beyond what has been presented. A little morbid but perhaps the only thing that could be interesting to do another film after one of the actors has actually passed away and examine loss head on.

I agree with this. I think the trilogy stands on its own. I think we are lucky they even made a third. Sometimes I wonder if part of it is as an audience we just want more. Someone told me they thought there should be a Darjeeling limited 2.

Something about that just felt so wrong. Yeah I’d like to see the three brothers go on another adventure but I don’t think that’s the point of the film.
This, or even before then, just as an exploration of old age and love.
She stated that after she was exhausted from producing her film, but she's still active in the industry now.
